scenarios.question: Tenant A stores a memory. An update tries to move metadata.user_id to tenant B. Which tenant can read the memory afterwards?
scenarios.hypothesis_title: update metadata can overwrite immutable tenant identity fields
scenarios.probe_action: Replay the memory update with identity metadata stripped and verify the original tenant retains access.
scenarios.recommendation: Restore immutable identity-scope enforcement so update metadata cannot overwrite or inject user_id, agent_id, run_id, or actor_id.

scenarios.question: A run-scoped memory is updated with user_id and agent_id metadata. Can the injected scopes read a memory that never belonged to them?
scenarios.hypothesis_title: update metadata can inject new identity scopes
scenarios.probe_action: Strip identity keys from update metadata and verify no new user or agent scope is granted.
scenarios.recommendation: Keep identity fields immutable after creation and reject or strip identity keys supplied through update metadata.

scenarios.question: A run-scoped memory is updated with camelCase userId and agentId aliases. Do those aliases grant a new tenant scope?
scenarios.hypothesis_title: camelCase identity aliases bypass metadata sanitization
scenarios.probe_action: Strip both snake_case and camelCase identity aliases, then verify only the original run scope resolves.
scenarios.recommendation: Sanitize both snake_case identity fields and camelCase aliases before persisting an update.

scenarios.question: A tenant updates only ordinary metadata such as category and priority. Does the memory remain readable by the original tenant?
A tenant updates metadata with its own unchanged user_id. Does the memory remain readable by that tenant?
A run-scoped memory is stored without an identity metadata update. Is it still isolated to its original run scope?
